title: Egebis Seyir User Guide
subtitle: Creating and editing Epics, Tasks, Sub-Tasks and Sprints — step by step, with pictures.

blocks.text: Seyir is a project management app where a team plans and tracks its work. This guide is written for someone who has never used it: at every step we point at the screen with red **numbered markers**. The number on the picture matches the list under the picture.
You only need to know a few words first:

head: Term
What it means
Example
rows: A work area for one product or team. All work items live inside a Project.
A big goal that gathers many Tasks under it. Optional.
One piece of work to do. It has a title, an owner, a date and points.
A small part of a Task. It cannot exist alone; it always belongs to a parent item.
A work period, usually 1–2 weeks, with a goal and dates. The team picks what to do in it.
The list of work not yet in a sprint, ordered by priority.
A score for the size of a piece of work (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55).

blocks.alt: Seyir home screen with marked areas
blocks.caption: Main screen: use the left menu for the Project and its sections, and the top bar for search, help and your account.
legend: **Project**: The project area you work in. Click to open the sections below it.
**Backlog and sprints**: Sprints are created and planned here.
**Sprint board**: Shows the sprint's work in status columns (Kanban).
**Tasks**: The Project's work list; Tasks and Sub-Tasks are added here.
**Search**: Find a task, document or person (shortcut: Ctrl + K).
**Help**: Open this guide at any time.
**Account menu**: Profile, language, theme and sign out.
**New item row**: Type a title and press Enter to add a task.

blocks.text: When you are stuck, click **Help** in the top bar. You can also get the Word version with **Download as Word** at the top right of the page.
Before you create Tasks and Sprints you need a Project to hold them. Your team lead usually prepares it for you, but it helps to know how it is done.

items: In the left menu click the **+** next to **SPACES** (or the **Create project** row at the bottom).
Type the Project's name in **Name** (e.g. Mobile App).
Check the **Key**. It is a short 2–10 letter code; item IDs start with it (MOB-1, MOB-2…). It is suggested automatically.
Optionally pick a colour and icon. Keep **Work mode** on **Scrum** to use Sprints and the Backlog, or choose **Kanban** for a continuous-flow board without sprints.
Click **Create project**.

blocks.caption: The new Project dialog. Keep the work mode on Scrum if you will use sprints.
legend: **Name**: The Project's display name.
**Key**: The short code at the start of item IDs (like MOB-1). It must not be used by another Project; keep it short and clear.
**Create project**: Saves and opens the Project.

blocks.text: A list called **Tasks** is created automatically inside the new Project. You will add your first Tasks there.

sections.title: 2. Epic: creating one and converting a Task into an Epic (optional)

blocks.text: An **Epic** is a big goal that gathers many Tasks under it (e.g. “User account management”). The hierarchy is: **Epic → Task → Sub-Task**. Using Epics is **optional**: in a small team you can work with Tasks directly, without any Epic.

items: An Epic does not enter a sprint; it stays as the umbrella. Tasks and Bugs are what go into a sprint.
An Epic's progress bar is calculated automatically from the status of the Tasks under it.
An Epic has no parent, and unlike Tasks and Sub-Tasks it carries no hour estimate or percentage.

blocks.text: **A) Creating an Epic from scratch**

items: In the left menu open your Project and click the **Tasks** list.
In the row at the bottom choose **Epic** in the **Type** box.
Type the title (e.g. “User account management”) and press **Enter**. The Epic is added to the list.

blocks.caption: To add an Epic choose Epic in the Type box, type a title, press Enter.
legend: **Type**: This should be **Epic**.
**Title**: The Epic's name; a short phrase for the big goal.
**Add ↵**: You can click this instead of pressing Enter.

blocks.text: To add a Task under an Epic, click the **⋯** button at the right of the Epic's row, choose **Add sub-item** and leave **Type** on **Task**.
**B) Converting an existing Task into an Epic**

The project was split into Epics and Tasks, but looking at one Task you realise the work is far too big. You do not have to delete it and start over: you can **convert it into an Epic in a few clicks**.

items: Click the **⋯** button at the right of the Task's row. (The same option is in the **⋯** menu of the Task's detail panel.)
Choose **Convert to Epic** from the menu.
Read what will change in the dialog and click **Convert to Epic**.
The Task is now an Epic; it shows with the Epic icon in the list.

blocks.alt: Convert to Epic option in the Task row menu
blocks.caption: Choose Convert to Epic from the Task's ⋯ menu.
legend: **⋯ (actions)**: Opens the Task's menu.
**Convert to Epic**: Makes this Task an Epic. Only shown on Tasks.

blocks.caption: The confirmation dialog explains what happens.
legend: **Question**: Shows which Task is being converted.
**Explanation**: Summarises what changes.
**Convert to Epic**: Confirms and converts.

blocks.caption: After the conversion: there are two Epics; the converted Epic's Sub-Task is now a Task.
legend: **Epic**: The Epic you created from scratch (purple bolt icon).
**Converted Epic**: It used to be a Task, now it is an Epic.
**Task**: It used to be a Sub-Task; it now sits under the Epic as a Task.

head: What happens in the conversion?
Description
rows: Task → **Epic**. Title, description, people, labels, dates, comments, attachments and dependencies stay as they are.
If the Task is under an Epic it is **detached** from it (an Epic has no parent).
If the Task is in a Sprint it **leaves the Sprint** (an Epic does not enter a Sprint). This is written to the Sprint history.
A Sub-Task cannot sit under an Epic, so all of them **become Tasks** under the Epic; their points are kept.
An Epic does not carry these, so they are **cleared**.

blocks.text: The conversion **cannot be undone**; you cannot turn the Epic back into a Task. Only a **Task** can be converted (not a Bug or Sub-Task) and the Project's work mode must be **Scrum**. Converting a Task that is in an active Sprint needs the Sprint planning permission.
A Task is one piece of work to do. The fastest way to add one is the add row at the bottom of the list.

items: In the left menu open your Project and click the **Tasks** list.
In the row at the bottom choose **Task** in the **Type** box.
Type the work's title in the next box (e.g. “Design the sign-in screen”). Keep it short and clear: it should say what must be done.
Press **Enter** (or click **Add ↵**). The task drops into the list and receives its ID (MOB-1).

blocks.alt: Quick add row for a Task
blocks.caption: The add row: choose the type, type a title, press Enter.
legend: **Type**: The kind of record to add. This guide uses **Task** (the other is Epic; Bugs are reported from the **Bugs** screen).
**Title**: The name of the work. To add several tasks, just press Enter after each title.
**Add ↵**: You can click this instead of pressing Enter.

blocks.text: To add many tasks in a row, type a title, press Enter, type the next, press Enter again. Fill in details (date, person, points) afterwards.
All details of a task are edited in the **detail panel** that opens from the right when you click its title. The panel has **no Save button**: a field is saved automatically when you change it.

items: In the list click the task's **title**. The detail panel opens from the right. (Use the expand icon at the top of the panel for a full page.)
Find the field you want to change (marked in the picture below) and pick or type a value.
When you are done, close the panel with the **X** at the top right. Nothing else is needed.

blocks.alt: Task detail panel and editable fields
blocks.caption: The task detail panel. Every marked row can be clicked and changed.
legend: **Title**: Click to rename.
**Status**: Where the work stands (Backlog, To do, In progress, In review…). Click and choose another.
**Priority**: Urgent, High, Normal or Low. Makes important work stand out.
**Assignee**: Who does the work. Click and pick one or more people.
**Due date**: When the work must be finished. Pick from the calendar or type a date.
**Story Point**: The size of the work. Only **1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55** can be chosen.
**Completion**: How much is done? Drag the slider (0–100%, in steps of 5).
**Description**: The details. Saved automatically as you type.

head: Field
What it is for
How to change it
rows: Shows the stage of the work; decides which column it sits in on the Kanban board.
Click the status badge in the panel or the list and choose a new status.
Click the badge and pick a priority.
Click the row and pick one or more people.
Planned dates. Unfinished work past its due date gets a red warning.
A size estimate; sprint totals are calculated from it.
Pick a value from the list (1–55).
How much is finished; it feeds the sprint progress.
Pick from the Labels row or type a new label.

blocks.alt: Changing the status from the list
blocks.caption: You can also change the status straight from the list without opening the panel.
legend: **Status badge**: Click to open the status list.
**New status**: Pick the status you want; the task updates instantly.

items: **Copy, archive and delete:** In the list click the **⋯** button at the right of the task. **Copy** makes a copy of the task, **Archive** hides it but keeps it, **Delete** sends it to the trash.
**If you deleted by mistake:** open **Settings → Archive and trash**, find the task and click **Restore**. Items in the trash are removed for good after a while.

blocks.text: If a Task has grown too big and has become an umbrella goal, use **Convert to Epic** in the same **⋯** menu (see the Epic section).

Only 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34 and 55 are valid Story Points; no other number can be entered. If the task has **Sub-Tasks** you cannot edit its points by hand, because its points are the sum of its sub-tasks (see Editing a Sub-Task).
Use a Sub-Task to split a big piece of work into parts. A Sub-Task always belongs to a parent (Task or Bug) and appears under it.

items: In the **Tasks** list click the **⋯** button at the right of the parent task's row.
Choose **Add sub-item** from the menu. A new add row opens under the task.
The type box is already on **Sub-task**. Type the title (e.g. “Draw the form fields”) and press **Enter**.
Keep typing and pressing Enter for more sub-tasks. When you are done, press **Esc** to close the row.

blocks.alt: Add sub-item option in the task row menu
blocks.caption: Choose Add sub-item from the parent's ⋯ menu.
legend: **⋯ (actions)**: Opens the task's menu.
**Add sub-item**: Lets you add a Sub-Task under this task.

blocks.caption: The sub-task add row: type Sub-task, write the title, press Enter.
legend: **Type**: This should be Sub-task.
**Title**: The sub-task's name; press Enter to add it.
**Add ↵**: You can click this instead of pressing Enter.

blocks.caption: Added sub-tasks appear indented right under the parent.
legend: **Expand/collapse arrow**: Shows or hides the sub-tasks.
**First sub-task** (MOB-4).
**Second sub-task** (MOB-5).

blocks.text: You can also add sub-tasks from the **Sub-items** section in the parent's detail panel. On the Backlog page, dragging a row onto another row and dropping it a bit to the right also makes it a **sub-task** of that row.
Sub-tasks do not enter a sprint on their own; they move together with their parent.
A sub-task is edited like any task: click its title and change the status, person, date, points and percentage in the detail panel. The difference is that its values flow up to the parent.

items: Click the sub-task's **title** (in the list or in the parent's **Sub-items** section).
Choose the **Story Point** value and, if needed, move the **Completion** slider.
To go back to the parent, click the **parent link** (e.g. MOB-1) above the title.

blocks.caption: The sub-task page: points and percentage are entered here.
legend: **Title**: The sub-task's name; click to change.
**Parent link**: Takes you to the item it belongs to.
**Story Point**: The sub-task's points (1–55).
**Completion**: The sub-task's percentage.

blocks.text: When you enter points and percentages on sub-tasks, the parent calculates its own from them:

blocks.caption: The parent's points are the sum of its sub-tasks (2 + 3 = 5) and cannot be edited by hand.
legend: **Sub-items**: The task's sub-tasks and their statuses.
**Story Point (locked)**: The sum of the sub-tasks; the list is disabled.
**Explanation note**: "Sum of the sub-tasks" says this field is calculated automatically.

items: **Points:** The parent's points = the sum of its sub-tasks' points. It updates by itself when you add, change or delete sub-tasks.
**Percentage:** The parent's percentage is the point-weighted average of its sub-tasks' percentages. A sub-task in a finished (Done) status counts as 100%.
**If you delete the sub-tasks:** the parent keeps its last points and can be edited by hand again.

blocks.text: To change a parent's points or percentage, change its sub-tasks' values; the field is locked on the parent.

sections.title: 7. Drag to make a Sub-Task or detach it

blocks.text: In the list you can drag a Task onto another Task to make it a Sub-Task, and drag a Sub-Task out to make it a standalone Task again. Only Tasks and Sub-Tasks can be moved.

items: Hover over a row; a **drag handle** (⋮⋮) appears at its far left.
Grab the handle and drag the Task onto the row of the **Task** it should go under; the target row is highlighted.
When you drop it a confirmation opens: “Make HTK-2 a Sub-Task of HTK-1?”. Click **Make Sub-Task**.
To detach a Sub-Task, start dragging it; a large **Detach** area appears at the bottom centre of the screen.
Drop the Sub-Task on **Detach** and confirm. It leaves its parent and becomes a standalone **Task**.

blocks.caption: The Detach area that appears while dragging a Sub-Task.
legend: **Dragged item**: The card you move with the mouse.
**Detach**: A Sub-Task dropped here becomes a standalone Task.

blocks.text: A Task that has Sub-Tasks cannot be moved under another Task; detach its Sub-Tasks first.

A sprint is the package of work the team chooses to do within a fixed time. Sprints are created on the **Backlog and sprints** page. To open it click **Backlog and sprints** under your Project in the left menu.

blocks.caption: The Backlog page: work not yet in a sprint is listed below.
legend: **Backlog and sprints**: Open this page from the left menu.
**Create sprint**: Opens the new sprint dialog.
**Backlog section**: All tasks not in a sprint, in priority order.

items: Click **Create sprint** at the top right.
Type the sprint's name in **Name** (e.g. Sprint 1).
In **Sprint goal** write in one sentence what will be achieved. (In some Projects the goal is required.)
Pick the **Start** and **End** dates. A two-week range is suggested; a sprint can last at most 8 weeks.
Optionally add a **Capacity note** (e.g. 3 people, one on leave for 2 days).
Click **Create sprint**. The sprint appears above the Backlog with the **Planned** status.

blocks.caption: The new sprint dialog and the fields to fill in.
legend: **Name**: The sprint's name.
**Sprint goal**: The purpose of this period; everyone sees it on the sprint header.
**Start**: First day.
**End**: Last day. It cannot be before the start; 8 weeks at most.
**Capacity note**: The team's situation in that period (leave, meetings…). Optional.
**Create sprint**: Saves the sprint.

head: Field
Required?
Description
rows: The name shown in lists and boards.
The team's shared aim. If left empty you get a warning when starting the sprint.
End cannot be before start; at most 8 weeks.

blocks.text: The sprint exists but is empty. You plan it by moving work from the Backlog into it. There are three ways; the menu is the easiest.

items: In the **Backlog** section click the **⋯** button at the right of the task you want to move.
Click **"Move to Sprint 1"**. The task moves under the sprint.
Repeat for the other tasks.

blocks.alt: Menu to move a task into a sprint
blocks.caption: Moving a task into a sprint: choose the sprint from the ⋯ menu.
legend: **⋯ (actions)**: The task's menu.
**Move to sprint**: Puts the task into the sprint you choose. To undo it, the same menu has **Move back to Backlog**.

items: **By dragging:** grab the handle at the left of the row and drop it on a sprint section. Moving between sprints and from a sprint back to the Backlog works the same way.
**Bulk move:** tick the boxes at the left of the rows and choose **Move to sprint…** from the bar that appears.
Tasks and Bugs can enter a sprint; Epics cannot. Sub-tasks come with their parent.

blocks.text: Adding or removing work in a sprint that has **already started (Active)** counts as a "scope change". Seyir asks you and shows it in the reports.
To change a sprint's name, goal, dates or capacity use the **⋯** menu on the sprint header.

items: Click the **⋯** button at the right of the sprint header.
Choose **Edit** from the menu. The "Edit sprint" dialog opens.
Update the field you want to change and click **Save**.

blocks.caption: The sprint menu: open the board, edit, export or delete.
legend: **Open Kanban board**: Shows the sprint's work in status columns.
**Edit**: Changes the sprint's details.
**Delete**: Deletes the sprint (only while it is **Planned**). Its work returns to the Backlog.

blocks.caption: The edit dialog has the same fields as the create dialog.
legend: **Name**: Changes the name.
**Sprint goal**: Updates the goal.
**End**: Extends or shortens the period. Dates are locked in an active sprint.
**Save**: Applies the changes.

blocks.text: On the sprint header you see its state at a glance and manage its life cycle:

blocks.caption: The sprint header: status, total points, percentage and breakdown by person.
legend: **Sprint name**: The header shows the name, date range and total points.
**Status**: Planned, Active, Completed or Cancelled.
**Percentage button**: Click to open or close the summary panel.
**Start**: Starts a planned sprint. In an active sprint **Complete** appears instead.
**Summary panel**: Total Story Points, done points, overall percentage and points/percentage per person.

items: **Start:** makes the sprint active. Seyir warns you if no goal is set or the sprint is empty.
**Complete:** asks what to do with unfinished work: **carry over to the next sprint** or **send to the Backlog**. Done points are recorded for the team's velocity.
**Cancel:** cancels the sprint and returns its work to the Backlog. This cannot be undone.
**Delete:** only a Planned sprint can be deleted.

blocks.text: To share a sprint choose **Copy link** from the menu; the link opens the sprint board directly. For reports use **Export to Excel** or **Download as JSON**.
Kanban is a board where work is tracked as cards in status columns. Open it by clicking **Sprint board** in the left menu or **Open Kanban board** in the sprint menu. Every sprint has its own board.

blocks.caption: The sprint board: columns are statuses, cards are tasks.
legend: **Sprint picker**: Choose which sprint's board to see.
**Card**: Task ID, title, points and percentage. Dragging a card to another column **changes its status**.
**Summary**: Opens the total points, percentage and breakdown by person.
**Start**: Starts a planned sprint.

items: To change a status without dragging, use **Change status** in the card's **⋯** menu.
The **flag** on a card is the priority, the number next to it is the **Story Point**, and the progress bar is the **completion percentage**.
The **Colour by priority** button above the board paints cards by priority (Urgent red, High orange…).

blocks.text: Bugs are not shown in the task list; they have their own screen. Open it with the red **Bugs** button at the top right of the sprint board (and the Kanban board). The number on the button is the count of open bugs.

items: Click the red **Bugs** button. (Or **New → Bug**.)
Click **Report a bug**. Fill in **What is wrong?**, **Severity**, **Priority**, **Steps to reproduce**, **Expected** and **Actual result**, **Environment**; add screenshots if you like.
Click **Report bug**. You become the **bug owner**; the bug starts as **Unassigned** and the people who assign bugs (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Admin) get a notification and an e-mail.
A Product Owner, Scrum Master or Admin assigns the bug in the **Assignee** box on its row. The status becomes **Assigned**; the assignee gets a notification and an e-mail.
The assignee sets the status to **In progress** when they start and **Resolved** when done. The bug owner is notified by e-mail at every change.

blocks.caption: The Bugs screen: status tabs, bug owner and assignee.
legend: **Bugs**: The screen opened by the red **Bugs** button on the sprint board.
**Report a bug**: Opens the new bug form.
**Status tabs**: Unassigned, Assigned, In progress, Resolved.
**Assignee**: Assigns the bug to someone (only people allowed to).

blocks.text: Click a bug to open its details in the side panel; add comments and files there.
The **New** button at the top of every page is the quickest way to start something. You do not have to open a list first.

items: Click **New** (or press **N** on the keyboard when you are not typing).
Pick what you want to create: **Task**, **Epic** or **Bug**. New Projects are created with the **Create project** button in the left menu.
For Task and Epic a small window opens (Bug opens the bug report form). Type the **Title** and check the **Project** and **List** (the one you are looking at is preselected).
Optionally click **Attach files** to add any files right away.
Click **Create**. The new item opens so you can fill in the details.

blocks.caption: The New menu opened from the top bar.
legend: **New**: The big button in the top bar. Shortcut: N.
**Task**: A piece of work for the sprint.
**Epic**: A big goal that groups many Tasks.

blocks.text: Sub-Tasks are created from inside a Task (**⋯ → Add sub-item**), because they always belong to a parent.

sections.title: 14. Sharing and permissions on a Task or Epic

blocks.text: By default every item follows the access of its Project. With **Share** you can add people or teams to one item (and everything under it) or make it **Private**.

items: Open the Task or Epic and click the big **Share** button at the top right.
To give someone more rights on this item only, choose them under **Add a person or team**, pick a role (for example **Developer**) and click **Add**.
To hide the item, switch on **Private**. Only the people listed (and Owners and Admins) will see it and everything under it.
Click **Save**. The button now says **Shared** or **Private**.
To go back to the Project rules, open **Share** again and click **Reset to inherited**.

blocks.caption: The Sharing and permissions window of an Epic.
legend: **Private**: Hides the item and everything under it from people who are not listed.
**Add a person or team**: Choose who gets access.
**Add**: Puts the person on the list with the selected role.
**Save**: Applies the settings.

blocks.text: Sub-Tasks and child Tasks **inherit** the settings of the item above them. A child can have its own settings, and then those win.
You cannot give someone more rights than you have yourself. To share an item with someone who is not in a private Project, first add them to that Project.
Administrators decide what each role can do in **Settings → Roles**. Changes apply immediately.

items: Open **Settings** and click **Roles**.
Choose **Project roles** (rights inside a Project) or **Workspace roles** (rights in the whole workspace).
Tick or untick a box to change a role. Each row is one permission.
Click **New role** to create your own role (for example **QA Engineer**). You can start from an existing role.
Use the **⋯** menu on a column to rename or delete a custom role, or reset a built-in role to its defaults.

blocks.caption: The Roles page with one column per role.
legend: **Project roles / Workspace roles**: Switches between the two kinds of roles.
**New role**: Creates a custom role.
**Role column**: One column per role; the number shows how many people use it.
**Check box**: Turns one permission on or off for that role.

blocks.text: Owners always keep every right, and a role cannot lose the permissions the workspace needs to keep running (for example Admins keep member and settings management).
You can attach files to any Task, Epic, Sub-Task or Bug, and to docs.

items: **Any file format** is accepted, up to **100 MB** each and 50 files per item.
Drag files onto the **Attachments** area, **paste** a screenshot from the clipboard, or click the area to browse.
You can also attach files in the **New** window while you create an item.
Images and PDFs open in a preview. Every other file (Office, zip, video, programs…) is downloaded, never opened in the browser.

blocks.text: Programs and scripts (like .exe) can be attached too, but they are only downloaded. Open them only if you trust the sender.

sections.title: 17. The Kanban board for a whole Project

blocks.text: Every Project has a **Kanban board** link in the left menu. It shows the open items of all the Project’s lists in one board. Choose **Kanban** as the work mode when you create a Project for a sprint-free, continuous flow.

items: In the left menu click **Kanban board** under your Project.
Each column is a status. Drag a card to another column to change its status.
Click **Add card** at the bottom of a column, type a title and press Enter to create a card in that status.
Use the **List**, filter box and **Only mine** to narrow the board. The **Rows** picker groups cards by assignee, Epic or priority.
A column with a limit shows a warning when it is full; the board never blocks you.

blocks.caption: The Kanban board with its filters and the Add card button.
legend: **List**: Show one list or all lists.
**Filter cards**: Narrow the board by title or ID.
**Kanban board**: Opens this board from the left menu. Use **Add card** at the bottom of a column to add cards.

blocks.text: Click a card’s title to open it in a side panel without leaving the board.

head: What do you want to do?
How?
rows: Click the search box or press **Ctrl + K**, then type the task name or ID (MOB-12).
In the task detail choose **Copy link** from the **⋯** menu (clicking the task ID in the Backlog also copies it). The address looks like /items/MOB-12.
Click **My work** in the left menu.
Turn a growing Task into an umbrella goal
Click the percentage button on the sprint header (Summary panel).
Account menu at the top right → **Language**.

blocks.text: **Frequently asked questions**

items: **Do I have to use Epics?** No. Epics are optional; you can work with Tasks directly.
**I cannot see Convert to Epic.** It only appears on Tasks, in Projects whose work mode is Scrum; it is not available on Bugs or Sub-Tasks. You also need write permission.
**Can I turn an Epic back into a Task?** No, the conversion cannot be undone. If you are unsure, copy the Task first and convert the copy.
**Why is there no 4 in the Story Point list?** Seyir uses the standard Fibonacci scale (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55). Choose the nearest value.
**Why can't I change the parent's points?** If it has sub-tasks, its points are their sum. Change the sub-tasks' points.
**I created a sprint but cannot see it.** Open **Backlog and sprints**; the sprint sits above the Backlog. You can also expand the arrow in the left menu to list sprints.
**I cannot put a Sub-Task straight into a sprint.** Sub-tasks move with their parent; move the parent to the sprint.
**Was my change not saved?** Seyir saves automatically; there is no Save button to look for.

blocks.text: If something is still unclear, contact your workspace admin. This guide is updated together with the app.
